mainTopic: End of the פרה אדומה discussion, the כהן גדול's second וידוי, and the משנה on the יום כיפור blood, coals, and קטורת
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion of the פרה אדומה. אביי explains that רבי יהודה really disagrees with the משנה even though his view is not recorded. The גמרא then learns from 'והזה הטהור על הטמא' that a טבול יום may sprinkle the פרה waters. רבי אסי adds that even רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש found no fixed pattern in these verses. They could only state the general rule of מַשְׁמָע מוֹצִיא מִיַּד מַשְׁמָע וּמַשְׁמָע מִמֵּילָא. רבי יוחנן rejects a ברייתא saying a זר may not slaughter the פרה, and he even disagrees with his own teacher on this point. The גמרא explains that the כהן גדול mentions the כהנים only in his second וידוי, because he must be atoned for first. A new משנה describes slaughtering the bull, stirring its blood, and scooping coals. It then lists many differences between a regular day and יום כיפור: the coal pan, the קטורת, the ramp, the washing, and the number of wood piles. The גמרא corrects the משנה so that the blood-stirrer stands outside the היכל, and it begins a ברייתא on 'וכל אדם לא יהיה באהל מועד' that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The משנה shows no disagreement from רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the משנה about who may sprinkle records no dissent from רבי יהודה. That is surprising, because his views elsewhere suggest he should disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה does not disagree!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a surprising fact: the משנה lists who may sprinkle the פרה waters, and רבי יהודה is not recorded as disagreeing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the סוגיא, רבי יהודה read the פרה verses differently from the חכמים. So we would expect him to argue about the sprinkling stage too. His silence in the משנה suggests he agrees, and that is the difficulty.

keyTerms.meaning: and not (here: an exclamation of surprise)

steps.confusionAlert: This line looks like a plain statement of fact, but it works as a challenge. The גמרא is surprised and expects an explanation.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda does not disagree!
phrases.notes: Said with surprise, and really meant as a question: how can it be that רבי יהודה doesn't argue?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא פְּלִיג רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion (on the previous amud) of the משנה listing who may sprinkle the פרה waters.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that רבי יהודה holds differently from the חכמים about who may do the פרה stages.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי יהודה disagreed, the משנה should have recorded his dissent. Its silence implies he agrees.

steps.title: אביי: by עולא's rule, רבי יהודה does disagree
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that, because of עולא's principle about how the verses' implications work, רבי יהודה necessarily disagrees, even though the משנה does not say so.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Since the Master (עולא) said, 'Sometimes what one verse implies cancels what an earlier verse implied, and sometimes what a verse implies stands on its own and carries forward,' רבי יהודה does disagree.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי resolves the challenge by saying that רבי יהודה really does disagree. His dissent simply was not written in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא taught that a requirement stated at one stage of the פרה may either cancel an earlier stage's rule or carry forward into later stages. Given that rule, רבי יהודה's reading of the earlier verse logically leads him to a different result at the sprinkling stage. So silence in the משנה does not prove agreement.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule of reading the verses is the key tool of this whole סוגיא. רבי אסי comes back to it in step 4.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Since the Master (Ulla) said:
'An implication takes away from an earlier implication,'
'and an implication can also stand on its own,'
he (Rabbi Yehuda) does disagree.
phrases.notes: The short answer: yes, he does argue, even though his opinion isn't written down here.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי כֵּיוָן דְּאָמַר מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the surprise raised in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Denies the inference from silence: the disagreement exists by logical necessity.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because the משנה is silent, רבי יהודה agrees.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because of עולא's rule, רבי יהודה's earlier reading forces him to disagree here too.

steps.title: A טבול יום may sprinkle the פרה אדומה waters
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads 'והזה הטהור על הטמא' and learns that a טבול יום is fit to sprinkle the פרה waters.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the pure one shall sprinkle upon the impure.' The word 'pure' implies that he was once impure. This teaches that a טבול יום is fit for the פרה service.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next verse and learns from the word 'הטהור' that a person who immersed today, but has not yet waited for nightfall, may sprinkle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier verse already required the sprinkler to be pure, so repeating 'pure' seems unnecessary. The extra word hints at someone who was impure and has only partly become pure, meaning a טבול יום. This is a special leniency of the פרה service.

keyTerms.meaning: one who immersed today but becomes fully pure only at nightfall

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean a טבול יום counts as fully טהור in general. It is a specific ruling that he is fit for the פרה service.

phrases.english: 'And the pure one shall sprinkle upon the impure.'
phrases.notes: Numbers 19:19

phrases.english: 'Pure', which implies that he was impure;
it teaches about one who immersed that day
that he is fit for the red heifer service.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִזָּה הַטָּהוֹר עַל הַטָּמֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the step-by-step reading of the פרה verses with the next verse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A טבול יום is fit to sprinkle the פרה waters.

steps.title: Even רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש found no clear pattern
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי reports that רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש worked hard on the פרה passage but gained very little. They could only state the general rule of מַשְׁמָע מוֹצִיא מִיַּד מַשְׁמָע וּמַשְׁמָע מִמֵּילָא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said: When רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש were working on the פרה passage, they got out of it only as much as a fox brings up from a plowed field. All they could say was: sometimes a verse's implication cancels an earlier one, and sometimes it stands on its own.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי closes the topic by admitting that the great אמוראים could not find a neat system here. They could only state the general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verses switch back and forth: some requirements carry forward to later stages, and some cancel earlier ones. רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש could not find a test for which is which, so each verse must be learned on its own. The fox image means very little was gained, like the bit of dirt a fox kicks up.

keyTerms.meaning: were engaged in it, were analyzing it

steps.whatToRemember: In the פרה verses, a requirement sometimes carries forward to later stages (מִמֵּילָא) and sometimes cancels an earlier one (מוֹצִיא מִיַּד). There is no fixed test for which applies; even רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש could only state the rule.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the סוגיא handles each stage one by one instead of with a single formula.

phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said:
When they were engaged in it,
Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish, in the passage of the red heifer,
they did not bring up from it
anything but as much as a fox brings up
from a plowed field.
Rather, they said:
'An implication takes away from an earlier implication,'
'and an implication can also stand on its own.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי כִּי הֲווֹ בַּהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ בְּפָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps back from the individual derivations and comments on the reading method used throughout.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פרה verses follow the rule 'מַשְׁמָע מוֹצִיא מִיַּד מַשְׁמָע וּמַשְׁמָע מִמֵּילָא' with no fixed pattern for which applies where.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Each stage of the פרה must be read on its own terms. The general rule is known, but there is no system for applying it.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the פרה אדומה cannot be slaughtered by a זר
steps.stepSummary: A תנא recites a ברייתא before רבי יוחנן. It says every שחיטה is valid by a זר except the שחיטה of the פרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A reciter of ברייתות taught in front of רבי יוחנן: All slaughterings are valid even if a non-כהן does them, except the slaughtering of the פרה אדומה.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא is quoted that makes the פרה אדומה an exception: only for it, a זר may not slaughter. This sets up רבי יוחנן's reaction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the שחיטה of a קרבן does not need a כהן. The עבודה that requires a כהן starts afterward, with receiving the blood. This ברייתא claims the פרה is different and needs a כהן even for the שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: a reciter in the בית מדרש who memorized ברייתות and recited them
The red heifer, whose ashes are used to purify from טומאת מת

phrases.english: A tanna recited before Rabbi Yochanan:
All slaughterings are valid when done by a non-kohen,
except that of the red heifer.
phrases.notes: The פרה is treated as an exception that needs a כהן.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי תַּנָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of the פרה אדומה with a new ברייתא about who may slaughter it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every שחיטה is valid by a זר except the שחיטה of the פרה אדומה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן rejects the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן tells the תנא to take the ברייתא outside, because no שחיטה is ever invalid by a זר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to him: Go out and teach that outside, not here. We have never found a case where slaughtering by a non-כהן is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן rejects the ברייתא completely. He holds that a זר may slaughter even the פרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reason is a general rule: שחיטה is never an עבודה that needs a כהן. Since we never find a שחיטה that is invalid by a זר, the פרה should be no different. Saying 'teach it outside' means the ברייתא is not reliable for the בית מדרש.

keyTerms.meaning: Go out and teach it outside, meaning this teaching is rejected here
We have not found; an argument from the absence of any such case

steps.confusionAlert: 'Go teach it outside' does not mean he is sending the student away. It is a sharp way of saying this ברייתא is not accepted.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said to him:
Go out and teach it outside:
We have not found a slaughtering by a non-kohen that is invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: פּוֹק תְּנִי לְבָרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the ברייתא quoted in step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The entire ברייתא's exception for the פרה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It goes against the general rule that שחיטה never needs a כהן.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן even disagreed with his own teacher on this
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows how firm רבי יוחנן was. He even disagreed with his teacher רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק, who held the same view as the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן did not listen to that תנא, and he did not even listen to his own teacher. רבי יוחנן reported in the name of רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק: The slaughter of the פרה by a non-כהן is invalid. And רבי יוחנן said: I say it is valid, because we never find a slaughtering that is invalid by a non-כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a comment: rejecting the תנא is not surprising, because רבי יוחנן even rejected his own teacher on this point. It proves this from a statement of רבי יוחנן himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'לא מיבעיא... אלא אפילו' build from a small claim to a bigger one. The proof is רבי יוחנן's own statement: he quotes his teacher saying 'invalid,' then disagrees with the same reason he gave the תנא. This shows his view was a firm principle.

keyTerms.meaning: Not only this... but even that; a build-up from small to big
And I say; a student stating his own opinion against what he just quoted

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן holds that a זר may slaughter even the פרה אדומה. His reason is that no שחיטה is ever invalid by a זר. He holds this against a ברייתא and even against his own teacher.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan,
needless to say that he did not listen to the tanna,
but even his own teacher he did not listen to.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוֹצָדָק:
phrases.english: As Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yehotzadak:
The slaughtering of the heifer by a non-kohen is invalid.
phrases.notes: This is the teacher's view, the same as the ברייתא.

phrases.english: And I say: it is valid,
phrases.notes: רבי יוחנן's own opinion.

phrases.english: for we have not found a slaughtering that is invalid by a non-kohen.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, לָא מִיבַּעְיָא לְתַנָּא דְּלָא צָיֵית, אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ לְרַבֵּיהּ לָא צָיֵית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens step 6 by showing רבי יוחנן held this view even against his teacher.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוחנן held firmly that the פרה may be slaughtered by a זר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's statement quoting רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק and then disagreeing with him.

steps.title: Why are the kohanim mentioned only in the second confession?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the כהן גדול's second confession on his bull. It asks why 'ובני אהרן עם קדושך' appears only in this second וידוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: He comes to his bull a second time. Why is it that in the first confession he did not say 'and the children of Aaron, Your holy people,' but in the second confession he did say it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה about the יום כיפור service. It asks why the wording of the two confessions is different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן גדול confesses over his own bull twice. The first time is for himself and his household. The second time is for himself, his household, and all the כהנים. The גמרא wants a reason why the כהנים are added only the second time.

keyTerms.meaning: Bull; here, the כהן גדול's own bull offering on יום כיפור
What is different? Asks for the reason behind a distinction
Your holy people; here referring to the כהנים

phrases.english: He comes next to his bull a second time.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה.

phrases.english: What is different about the first confession
in which he did not say: "and the children of Aaron, Your holy people,"
and what is different about the second confession
in which he did say: "and the children of Aaron, Your holy people"?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּא לוֹ אֵצֶל פָּרוֹ שְׁנִיָּה. מַאי שְׁנָא בְּוִידּוּי רִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the פרה discussion and returns to the משנה of the יום כיפור service.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the כהנים are included only in the second וידוי.

steps.title: An innocent person should atone for the guilty
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי ישמעאל explains that justice requires the כהן גדול to gain atonement for himself first. Only then can he atone for the other כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: This is what fairness requires. It is better that someone who is innocent come and atone for the guilty, and not that someone guilty come and atone for the guilty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a teaching from דבי רבי ישמעאל. The כהן גדול first atones for himself, so that he is 'innocent' when he atones for the other כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the first וידוי, the כהן גדול has not yet gained atonement, so he is still 'guilty.' Once the first וידוי has atoned for him and his household, he is now a זכאי. That is why the כהנים are added only in the second וידוי.

keyTerms.meaning: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught; introduces a ברייתא from his academy
The attribute of justice, what fairness requires
Innocent; one who has already gained atonement
Guilty; one who still needs atonement

steps.whatToRemember: The כהן גדול first gains atonement for himself and his household. Only then, as a זכאי, does he atone for the other כהנים. That is why 'ובני אהרן עם קדושך' appears only in the second וידוי.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
This is what the attribute of justice dictates:
Better that an innocent one should come
and atone for the guilty one,
and let a guilty one not come
and atone for the guilty one.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל, כָּךְ הִיא מִדַּת הַדִּין נוֹתֶנֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The כהן גדול must first be atoned for himself, so that as a זכאי he can atone for the guilty כהנים in the second וידוי.

steps.title: Slaughtering the bull and stirring its blood
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה begins: the כהן גדול slaughters his bull, catches its blood in a bowl, and hands it to a helper. The helper stirs it on the fourth row of the היכל so it does not clot.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: He slaughtered the bull and caught its blood in a bowl. He gave it to someone who stirs it, standing on the fourth row of tiles in the היכל, so that it does not clot.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. It continues the order of the יום כיפור service right after the second וידוי on the bull.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blood will only be sprinkled later, after the כהן גדול offers the קטורת inside. Meanwhile it must stay liquid, so a helper keeps stirring it. Clotted blood cannot be sprinkled properly.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מַתְנִיתִין, 'our משנה'. It marks the start of a new משנה.
A bowl used to catch the blood of a קרבן.
A row of floor tiles or paving stones.

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the order of the service. Slaughter comes first, then the קטורת is brought inside, and only after that is the blood sprinkled. That is why the blood has to be kept liquid in the meantime.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
phrases.notes: A new משנה begins here.

phrases.english: He slaughtered it and received its blood in a bowl,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the כהן גדול's own bull, the one he just confessed on.

phrases.english: and gives it to the one who stirs it
on the fourth row of tiles in the Sanctuary,
phrases.notes: The way the משנה words it, the helper seems to stand inside the היכל. In step 26 the גמרא changes it to 'של היכל': the fourth row counted outward from the היכל's entrance, outside the building.

phrases.english: so that it does not congeal.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ שְׁחָטוֹ וְקִבֵּל בְּמִזְרָק אֶת דָּמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The previous discussion explained the wording of the second וידוי. Now a new משנה continues the service from that point: the bull is slaughtered.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול slaughters the bull and catches its blood. A helper stirs the blood on the fourth row of the היכל so it stays liquid until it is sprinkled. The גמרא clarifies that this row is outside the היכל.

steps.title: Scooping coals from the altar
steps.stepSummary: The כהן גדול takes a coal pan, climbs the מזבח, moves the outer coals aside, and scoops the well-burned inner coals. He then comes down and sets the pan on the fourth row of the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He took a coal pan and went up to the top of the מזבח. He moved the coals to this side and that side and scooped from the well-burned inner coals. Then he came down and placed the pan on the fourth row of tiles in the עזרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה describes how the כהן גדול gets the burning coals he will use for the קטורת inside קודש הקדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not just grab the top coals. He pushes them aside and takes from the inner coals, which are fully burned and glowing. Then he puts the pan down so he can prepare the קטורת next.

keyTerms.meaning: A coal pan or fire pan used to carry coals.
The courtyard of the בית המקדש.

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different 'fourth rows' in this משנה. The blood is stirred on the fourth row of the היכל, which the גמרא explains is counted outward from the היכל's entrance (step 26). The coal pan is set down on the fourth row in the עזרה, which is the outer courtyard.

phrases.english: He took a coal pan and ascended to the top of the altar,
phrases.notes: This is the outer מזבח, in the courtyard.

phrases.english: and cleared coals to this side and that side,
and scoops from the inner, well-burned coals,
and he descended and placed it
on the fourth row of tiles in the courtyard.
phrases.notes: Notice: here it is the עזרה, not the היכל.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָטַל מַחְתָּה וְעָלָה לְרֹאשׁ הַמִּזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It continues the same משנה's order of service. After the slaughter comes gathering the coals for the קטורת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול scoops the inner, fully burned coals from the top of the מזבח and sets the pan down in the עזרה.

steps.title: Silver pan every day, gold pan on יום כיפור
steps.stepSummary: On a regular day, the כהן scoops with a silver pan and pours the coals into a gold pan. On יום כיפור, the כהן גדול scoops with a gold pan and brings that same pan inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: Every day he would scoop with a silver pan and pour the coals into a gold one. Today (יום כיפור) he scoops with a gold pan, and with it he would bring the coals inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה begins a list of contrasts between the daily coal pan and the יום כיפור coal pan. This first one is about the metal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a regular day, two pans are used, with a transfer from silver to gold. On יום כיפור, only one gold pan is used from start to finish. No pouring takes place, and the same pan goes into קודש הקדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Every day … but today'. This is the pattern that contrasts the regular days with יום כיפור.
Pours, empties from one vessel into another.
Brings inside. Here it means into קודש הקדשים.

phrases.aramaic: בְּכׇל יוֹם הָיָה חוֹתֶה בְּשֶׁל כֶּסֶף
phrases.english: Every day he would scoop with one of silver
phrases.notes: 'One of silver' means a silver coal pan.

phrases.english: and pour into one of gold,
but today he scoops with one of gold
phrases.notes: 'Today' means יום כיפור.

phrases.english: and with it he would bring in.
phrases.notes: He brings the same pan into קודש הקדשים.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּכׇל יוֹם הָיָה חוֹתֶה בְּשֶׁל כֶּסֶף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After describing the scooping, the משנה contrasts how the scooping is done on a regular day with how it is done on יום כיפור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On יום כיפור, a single gold coal pan is used for both scooping and bringing in. There is no transfer from silver to gold.

steps.title: Four-קבין pan every day, three-קבין pan on יום כיפור
steps.stepSummary: On a regular day, the כהן scoops with a pan holding four קבין and pours into a pan of three קבין. On יום כיפור, he scoops with a three-קבין pan and brings it in directly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Every day he scoops with a pan of four קבין and pours into a pan of three קבין. Today he scoops with a pan of three קבין, and with it he would bring the coals in.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second contrast, about the size of the pan. This is the opinion of the unnamed תנא, the תנא קמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a regular day, the bigger scooping pan holds more coals than the smaller pan it is poured into. On יום כיפור, he scoops directly with the smaller pan. Again, there is no pouring between pans.

phrases.aramaic: בְּכׇל יוֹם חוֹתֶה בְּשֶׁל אַרְבַּעַת קַבִּין
phrases.english: Every day he scoops with one of four kav
and pours into one of three kav,
but today he scoops with one of three kav
and with it he would bring in.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּכׇל יוֹם חוֹתֶה בְּשֶׁל אַרְבַּעַת קַבִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the next item in the same list of daily-versus-יום כיפור contrasts. It moves from the metal to the size.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the תנא קמא, the daily scooping pan holds four קבין and is poured into a three-קבין pan. On יום כיפור, a three-קבין pan is used directly.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: the daily pan held a סאה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי disagrees only about the size of the daily scooping pan. He says it held a סאה, which is six קבין. He agrees that on יום כיפור a three-קבין pan is used.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: every day he scoops with a pan of a סאה and pours into a pan of three קבין. Today he scoops with a pan of three קבין, and with it he would bring the coals in.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי gives a different version of the size contrast. His disagreement is only about the regular days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree about יום כיפור: a three-קבין pan is used to scoop and bring in. They disagree only about the daily scooping pan. The תנא קמא says four קבין, and רבי יוסי says a סאה, which is six קבין.

keyTerms.meaning: A larger unit of volume, equal to six קבין.

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי does not argue about יום כיפור at all. Only the size of the everyday scooping pan is in dispute.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
Every day he scoops with one of a se'a
phrases.notes: A סאה is six קבין.

phrases.english: and pours into one of three kav,
but today he scoops with one of three kav
phrases.notes: This is the same as the תנא קמא.

phrases.english: and with it he would bring in.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: בְּכׇל יוֹם חוֹתֶה בְּשֶׁל סְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יוסי offers a different measurement for the daily pan described in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי, the daily scooping pan held a סאה, which is six קבין. On יום כיפור, a three-קבין pan is used.

steps.title: Weight, handle, and color of the יום כיפור pan
steps.stepSummary: On a regular day, the pan was heavy, had a short handle, and was made of greenish gold. On יום כיפור, it was light, had a long handle, and was made of red gold. These are the words of רבי מנחם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Every day it was heavy, but today it was light. Every day its handle was short, but today it was long. Every day its gold was greenish, but today it was red. These are the words of רבי מנחם.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its list of contrasts with three more differences in the pan itself. All three are attributed to רבי מנחם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These changes make the יום כיפור pan easier for the כהן גדול to carry. It is lighter, and its long handle lets him support it with his arm. It is also made of a finer, red gold. The closing words 'דברי רבי מנחם' tell us whose list this is.

keyTerms.meaning: Greenish, describing a lesser grade of gold.
Red, describing a finer grade of gold.

steps.whatToRemember: On יום כיפור, the כהן גדול uses one special coal pan for the whole job. It is gold, holds three קבין, is light, has a long handle, and is made of red gold. On regular days, the coals are scooped with one pan and poured into another.

phrases.aramaic: בְּכׇל יוֹם הָיְתָה כְּבֵדָה, וְהַיּוֹם קַלָּה.
phrases.english: Every day it was heavy, but today it was light.
phrases.notes: A lighter pan so the כהן גדול does not get tired.

phrases.aramaic: בְּכׇל יוֹם הָיְתָה יָדָהּ קְצָרָה, וְהַיּוֹם אֲרוּכָּה.
phrases.english: Every day its handle was short, but today it was long.
phrases.notes: A long handle lets him rest it against his arm.

phrases.aramaic: בְּכׇל יוֹם הָיְתָה זֶהָבָה יָרוֹק, וְהַיּוֹם אָדוֹם.
phrases.english: Every day its gold was greenish, but today red.
These are the words of Rabbi Menachem.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּכׇל יוֹם הָיְתָה כְּבֵדָה, וְהַיּוֹם קַלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It finishes the list of daily-versus-יום כיפור contrasts, moving from size to weight, handle, and color.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מנחם, the יום כיפור pan is light, has a long handle, and is made of red gold. The daily pan is heavy, has a short handle, and is made of greenish gold.

steps.title: Extra handful of incense on יום כיפור
steps.stepSummary: Every day a פרס of קטורת is offered in the morning and another פרס in the afternoon. On יום כיפור a full handful is added.
steps.simpleTranslation: Every day the כהן offers half a מנה of incense in the morning and half a מנה in the afternoon. Today, the כהן גדול adds his full handful.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists another difference between a regular day and יום כיפור, this time about how much קטורת is offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The daily amount is one מנה, split into two halves called פרס. On יום כיפור nothing is taken away from that. Instead, the כהן גדול adds a full handful, which he burns inside the קודש הקדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: Afternoon (the time of the afternoon offering)
His two hands full, a double handful

phrases.english: Every day he offers half a maneh in the morning
phrases.notes: פרס means half of the one-מנה amount offered each day.

phrases.english: and half a maneh in the afternoon,
and today he adds his full handful.
phrases.notes: This handful is burned inside the קודש הקדשים

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּכׇל יוֹם מַקְרִיב פְּרָס בְּשַׁחֲרִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of 'every day versus today' contrasts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On יום כיפור, a full handful of קטורת is added on top of the regular daily amount.

steps.title: Extra-fine incense on יום כיפור
steps.stepSummary: The daily קטורת is fine. On יום כיפור it is ground even finer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Every day the incense was fine, and today it was the finest of the fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds that the קטורת used on יום כיפור is ground more finely than usual.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה requires all קטורת to be finely ground. For the incense brought into the קודש הקדשים, an extra level of grinding was done. This is a step above the normal requirement.

phrases.english: Every day it was fine,
and today it was finest of the fine.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּכׇל יוֹם הָיְתָה דַּקָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of the קטורת, moving from its amount to its quality.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The יום כיפור קטורת must be ground extra fine.

steps.title: How the כהן גדול walks on the ramp
steps.stepSummary: Regular כהנים go up the east side of the ramp and come down the west side. On יום כיפור the כהן גדול goes up and comes down the middle.
steps.simpleTranslation: Every day, the כהנים go up on the eastern side of the ramp and come down on its western side. Today, the כהן גדול goes up in the middle and comes down in the middle.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists a difference in how the כבש, the ramp to the מזבח, is used on יום כיפור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the כהנים use the ramp like a one-way path: up on one side and down on the other. On יום כיפור the כהן גדול walks straight up and down the center. This is the view of the first תנא, the unnamed opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: The ramp leading up to the מזבח

phrases.aramaic: בְּכׇל יוֹם כֹּהֲנִים עוֹלִין בְּמִזְרָחוֹ שֶׁל כֶּבֶשׁ
phrases.english: Every day the priests ascend on the eastern side of the ramp
and descend on its western side,
and today the High Priest ascends in the middle
and descends in the middle.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּכׇל יוֹם כֹּהֲנִים עוֹלִין בְּמִזְרָחוֹ שֶׁל כֶּבֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new item in the list of differences.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the first תנא, the כהן גדול uses the middle of the ramp on יום כיפור only.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the middle of the ramp all year
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the כהן גדול always walks up and down the middle of the ramp.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: The כהן גדול always goes up in the middle and comes down in the middle.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with the first תנא and says this is not a special יום כיפור practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, walking in the middle is part of the כהן גדול's honor every day of the year. So on this point, יום כיפור is not different. The word לעולם ('always') signals the disagreement.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה does not deny that the כהן גדול walks in the middle on יום כיפור. He agrees with that. He only adds that the כהן גדול does it every other day too.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
The High Priest always ascends in the middle
and descends in the middle.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: לְעוֹלָם כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל עוֹלֶה בָּאֶמְצַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with Step 18 about whether the middle-of-the-ramp rule is special to יום כיפור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול always uses the middle of the ramp, every day of the year.

steps.title: Washing from the golden flask on יום כיפור
steps.stepSummary: Every day the כהן גדול washes his hands and feet from the כיור. On יום כיפור he washes from a golden flask.
steps.simpleTranslation: Every day the כהן גדול sanctifies his hands and feet from the laver. Today, he does it from the golden flask.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists another difference: where the כהן גדול washes before doing the service.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the כהן גדול washes from the כיור, the large basin, like every other כהן. On יום כיפור, out of honor for him, he washes from a special golden flask instead.

keyTerms.meaning: Washes and sanctifies his hands and feet before the service
The large copper basin (laver) in the עזרה

phrases.aramaic: בְּכׇל יוֹם כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל מְקַדֵּשׁ יָדָיו וְרַגְלָיו
phrases.english: Every day the High Priest sanctifies his hands and his feet
from the laver,
and today from the golden flask.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּכׇל יוֹם כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל מְקַדֵּשׁ יָדָיו וְרַגְלָיו מִן הַכִּיּוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new item in the list, with the same structure as Step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the first תנא, the golden flask is used only on יום כיפור.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the golden flask all year
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the כהן גדול always washes from the golden flask.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: The כהן גדול always sanctifies his hands and feet from the golden flask.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה again disagrees and says this practice is not unique to יום כיפור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as his view about the ramp. For רבי יהודה, honoring the כהן גדול applies all year, so the golden flask is his everyday washing vessel.

keyTerms.meaning: Flask, the vessel רבי יהודה says the כהן גדול always uses

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה is consistent: both the middle of the ramp and the golden flask are special honors for the כהן גדול every day, not only on יום כיפור.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: לְעוֹלָם כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל מְקַדֵּשׁ יָדָיו וְרַגְלָיו
phrases.english: The High Priest always sanctifies his hands and his feet
from the golden flask.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: לְעוֹלָם כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל מְקַדֵּשׁ יָדָיו וְרַגְלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with Step 20, following the same pattern as Step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול always washes from the golden flask.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: four wood piles daily, five today
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says there were four מערכות on the מזבח every day and five on יום כיפור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Every day there were four wood arrangements there, and today five. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists a difference in the number of wood piles on the מזבח. It starts with רבי מאיר's count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מערכה is a separate pile of burning wood on the מזבח, each with its own job. On יום כיפור one more pile is added, for the coals the כהן גדול scoops to bring inside with the קטורת. The גמרא later explains which piles each תנא counts.

keyTerms.meaning: Arrangements, meaning piles of wood burning on the מזבח

phrases.aramaic: בְּכׇל יוֹם הָיוּ שָׁם אַרְבַּע מַעֲרָכוֹת,
phrases.english: Every day there were four arrangements there,
and today five,
the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּכׇל יוֹם הָיוּ שָׁם אַרְבַּע מַעֲרָכוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new item in the list, which opens a three-way disagreement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: four piles daily, five on יום כיפור.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: three wood piles daily, four today
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי counts one fewer pile: three every day and four on יום כיפור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: Every day three, and today four.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי gives a different count of the wood piles.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי agrees that יום כיפור adds exactly one pile. He disagrees with רבי מאיר only about one of the everyday piles, which he does not count.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
Every day three, and today four.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: בְּכׇל יוֹם שָׁלֹשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי מאיר's count in Step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי: three piles daily, four on יום כיפור.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: two wood piles daily, three today
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה gives the lowest count: two piles every day and three on יום כיפור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: Every day two, and today three.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה gives the third and smallest count of wood piles. This ends the three-way disagreement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each תנא counts one fewer everyday pile than the one before. All three still agree that יום כיפור adds exactly one extra pile. The disagreement is only about the everyday count.
steps.whatToRemember: The count goes 4/5 for רבי מאיר, 3/4 for רבי יוסי, and 2/3 for רבי יהודה. Everyone agrees יום כיפור has one more pile than a regular day.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Every day two, and today three.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: בְּכׇל יוֹם שְׁתַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third count, completing the disagreement begun in Step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: two piles daily, three on יום כיפור.

steps.title: How can the stirrer stand inside the היכל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה, which places the blood-stirrer inside the היכל, using the פסוק that no person may be in the אהל מועד during the כהן גדול's עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: But it is written: "And no person shall be in the Tent of Meeting"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by questioning the משנה. The משנה says the helper stirs the blood on the fourth row inside the היכל. But a פסוק seems to forbid anyone from being there at that time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the כהן גדול goes in to do the כפרה, the פסוק says no one may be in the אהל מועד. The היכל counts as part of the אהל מועד. So how could the משנה put the stirrer on a row of floor tiles inside the היכל?

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains and analyzes the משנה
"But it is written!" A challenge from a פסוק
The Tent of Meeting. In the בית המקדש, this includes the היכל
A row of floor tiles, used in the משנה to mark where the stirrer stood

phrases.english: GEMARA: But is it not written:
phrases.notes: This is how the גמרא starts a question from a פסוק.

phrases.english: "And no man shall be in the Tent of Meeting"?
phrases.notes: ויקרא טז:יז, said about the time when the כהן גדול goes in to make atonement.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָכְתִיב: ״וְכׇל אָדָם לֹא יִהְיֶה בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns back to the משנה's detail about the blood-stirrer standing on the fourth row in the היכל.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that the stirrer stands on the fourth row inside the היכל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק forbids any person from being in the אהל מועד during the כהן גדול's עבודה. The היכל is part of the אהל מועד, so no one should be standing there.

steps.title: רב יהודה: read it as the fourth row belonging to the היכל
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה corrects the wording of the משנה. The stirrer stands on the fourth row "of the היכל," meaning outside it, counting out from its entrance.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: Teach it as "of the היכל."
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the challenge by changing one word in the משנה. Instead of "in the היכל," read "of the היכל."
steps.deeperAnalysis: "In the היכל" meant inside, which the פסוק forbids. "Of the היכל" means the fourth row measured from the היכל's entrance, outside the building. So the stirrer is not inside the אהל מועד, and the פסוק is not broken.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sanctuary building, in front of the קודש הקדשים
"Of the היכל". Here it means outside, counted from its entrance

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read "שֶׁל הֵיכָל" as "inside the היכל." The whole point of the fix is that the stirrer stands outside, on the fourth row counted out from the היכל.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
Teach it as: "of the Sanctuary."
phrases.notes: The fourth row belonging to the היכל, which is outside, counted from its entrance.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: תְּנִי ״שֶׁל הֵיכָל״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the פסוק by correcting the wording of the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה placed the stirrer inside the היכל, which would go against the פסוק.
steps.terutzMaskana: The stirrer stands outside the היכל, on the fourth row from its entrance. So he is not in the אהל מועד.
steps.whatToRemember: The blood-stirrer stood outside the היכל, because no one may be in the אהל מועד while the כהן גדול does the עבודה inside.

steps.title: A ברייתא begins to explain the פסוק about no person in the אהל מועד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that quotes ״וכל אדם לא יהיה באהל מועד״, setting up a closer look at this rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: "And no man shall be in the Tent of Meeting"...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It quotes a ברייתא that is about to explain the same פסוק in more detail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that we know the פסוק matters for where people may stand, the ברייתא will explain how far the rule reaches. This line only quotes the פסוק. The explanation comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching from the time of the תנאים that is not in the משנה
"Any man". The ברייתא will explain who this includes

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
"And no man shall be in the Tent of Meeting,"
phrases.notes: The ברייתא quotes the פסוק and will explain it on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״וְכׇל אָדָם לֹא יִהְיֶה בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that explains the same פסוק used in the challenge.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק ״וכל אדם לא יהיה באהל מועד״ is the source for keeping everyone out of the אהל מועד during the כהן גדול's עבודה. The details continue on the next amud.
